question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>:</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>→</mo><mi>R</mi></math> be defined by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>min</mi><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> is the greatest integer less than or equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> denote the set containing all <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi></math> is discontinuous, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> denote the set containing all <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi></math> is not differentiable. Then the sum of number of elements in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> is equal to _____.

solution.text:
Given,

fx=minx-x,1+x-x

So, the graph of the function is 

1-x=1-x;0≤x<1

From the graph we can say that the function is continuous at all points in the interval 0,3.

So, P=0

Again, from the diagram, we can say that at x=12,1,32,2,52, there are sharp edges.

So, the function is non differentiable at x=12,1,32,2,52

Hence, Q=5

So, P+Q=5
